clauses.reason: Terminated by statutory repeal on 1935-06-14. The operative paragraph approves the amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry and modifies the previous approval to include approval of the code in its entirety as amended. The order states no period, condition or date of its own, so it has no own-terms end. Its operative effect depended on section 3 of Title I: under 3(b) the approved code's provisions became the standards of fair competition for the trade, a violation in or affecting interstate commerce was an unfair method of competition, under 3(c) the district courts could restrain violations and under 3(f) a violation was a misdemeanor. Section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 (49 Stat. 375, chapter 246, approved June 14, 1935) provides 'All the provisions of Title I of such Act delegating power to the President to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition and providing for the enforcement of such codes are hereby repealed' and states no later effective date, so the approval's prospective operative effect ended when the resolution was approved. Actor: the Congress by Senate Joint Resolution 113. The date is the resolution's approval date, not a general rule's default: the repeal reaches this command because the command had legal effect only through the repealed provisions. June 16, 1935 is not an end (section 1 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936). Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization recorded in source_notes, not an end date.

research_rationale:
Text and identity: EO 6756D is read in full in the registered American Presidency Project (APP) transcription jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-6756-d-approval-amendments-the-code-fair-competition-for-the-distilled.txt (grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held; replace and re-check quotes when an official copy is retrieved). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-29: the row with the same sha256 (3b2f583c2737...) in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl is a common-crawl capture (CC-MAIN-2025-47, captured 2025-11-13T07:00:08Z, WARC location recorded so the page can be re-fetched) whose heading is 'Executive Order 6756-D—Approval of Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry' and whose date is 1934-06-29; that date agrees with the date line of the held text ('June 29, 1934.'), and the row's text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held file is the whole order (recital, operative paragraph, signature, the Administrator's recommendation and the date line); it carries no order number, so the number comes from the page record. Clauses and sources are quoted from this registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. Identity: number, date and subject agree across the APP page record, the census register ('Executive Order 6756-D—Approval of Amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry', 1934-06-29) and the WPA 1944 numbered list (printed page 583: 'Amendments to Code of Fair Competition for the Dis tilledSpiritsIndustry approved.'). The WPA list says the order approves amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry. EO 6756-D (June 29, 1934, Franklin D. Roosevelt) recites that the Federal Alcohol Control Administration submitted amendments to the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry with its report, finds in five numbered paragraphs that the application, notice, hearings and statutory conditions were met, and then orders: 'do hereby approve said Amendments and modify my previous approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Industry by Executive Order dated November 26, 1933, to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended.' The machine inventory was wrong (it made clauses of the five findings and omitted the operative paragraph), so the inventory is corrected to the one operative paragraph. Legal reading: a section 3(a) approval of amendments, with a modification of the earlier approval of the code, and no period or date of its own. Its operative effect ended with the repeal on 1935-06-14. Later orders approving further amendments to the same code (EO 6811, August 4, 1934; EO 7000, April 5, 1935; EO 7018, April 19, 1935) each state that they approve an amendment and 'modify my previous approval ... to include an approval of said Code in its entirety as hereby amended'; under the owner's 2026-10-21 strike-and-insert ruling an amendment is a later event on the continuing approval, not an end. They are not attached to this packet as evidence records, so they are described here and not cited as events.

Orders for which no text is held (for example EO 6454) could not be searched, so the search covers held texts only. savings.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the code while the approval was in force are accrued effects, and the section 5 antitrust exemption for action complying with the approved code taken while Title I was in effect (and for sixty days after) is an accrued effect for that completed action. The proviso to section 2 of Senate Joint Resolution 113 narrows the exemption to agreements and action thereunder that put section 7(a) requirements into effect or prohibit practices already unlawful; it names agreements, states no time limit, and the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the exemption for action under codes before June 14, 1935. No held source shows a prosecution continued after June 14, 1935, and none continues the approval itself. The amendments approved here were part of the approved code only while the approval stood; later amendment orders are separate later events.
